sources.name: SportsMOT
sources.contents: 240 sports clips (basketball, football, volleyball); basketball subset averages ~845 frames and ~10 tracks per clip; MOT-format player boxes and track IDs.
sources.attribution_text: Cui et al., SportsMOT: A Large Multi-Object Tracking Dataset in Multiple Sports Scenes, ICCV 2023.
sources.retrieval_method: Gated Hugging Face download or Codalab registration; no redistribution.
sources.notes: Best public basketball MOT benchmark. Align our MOT export with its format and use TrackEval for HOTA/IDF1/MOTA.

sources.name: MultiSports
sources.contents: ~3,200 clips across 4 sports including basketball; 66 fine-grained action classes with spatio-temporal tubelets; ~37,701 instances / 902k boxes.
sources.attribution_text: Li et al., MultiSports: A Multi-Person Video Dataset of Spatio-Temporally Localized Sports Actions, ICCV 2021.
sources.retrieval_method: Gated Hugging Face download; basketball tarball available.
sources.notes: Closest public benchmark for action localization; useful for event-tubelet ideas, not for commercial release.

sources.name: DeepSportRadar basketball-instants-dataset
sources.contents: 700+ high-resolution multi-camera image pairs with ball/player keypoints, segmentation masks, and camera calibration.
sources.attribution_text: Van Zandycke et al., DeepSportradar-v1, ACM MMSports 2022.
sources.retrieval_method: Kaggle download after login.
sources.notes: Strong for calibration and keypoint work. Challenge terms and no-redistribution conditions may add restrictions.

sources.name: Basketball-51
sources.contents: 10,311 six-second clips from 51 broadcast games, 320x240, labeled by shot outcome (2pt/3pt/FT/mid-range, make/miss).
sources.attribution_text: Shakya, Zhang, Zhou, Basketball-51: A Video Dataset for Activity Recognition in the Basketball Game, CS & IT Conference Proceedings 2021.
sources.retrieval_method: Kaggle download after login.
sources.notes: Kaggle license says Apache-2.0, but the clips are broadcast-derived. Treat the stated license as self-asserted until provenance is cleared.

sources.name: BASKET: A Large-Scale Video Dataset for Fine-Grained Skill Estimation
sources.contents: 4,477 hours of basketball video, 32,232 players, 21 leagues, 20 skill labels; long highlight videos per player.
sources.attribution_text: Pan, Zhang, Bertasius, BASKET: A Large-Scale Video Dataset for Fine-Grained Skill Estimation, CVPR 2025.
sources.retrieval_method: Gated Hugging Face download after accepting terms.
sources.notes: Contains NBA/NCAA/FIBA broadcast footage. Do not treat the card's Apache-2.0 metadata as commercial clearance for the underlying video.

sources.name: PL-NBA: Possession-level Universal Basketball Video Dataset
sources.contents: 40 NBA games, 7,000+ offensive possession clips, 30,000+ fine-grained events; annotations only, video must be obtained separately.
sources.attribution_text: PL-NBA dataset authors (holhouse).
sources.retrieval_method: GitHub annotation download; video must be sourced independently and lawfully.
sources.notes: Do not scrape NBA video to pair with these annotations. Useful for schema design and research-only evaluation.

sources.name: BasketEvent
sources.contents: ~35K videos, 90.6 hours of NBA broadcast footage, 51K player-level samples, 10 event categories (made/missed shot, FT, foul, turnover, jump ball, rebound, steal, block, assist), game-level splits, 1K temporal subset.
sources.attribution_text: Zhang, Rao, Wu, Xie, BasketEvent, BMVC 2026.
sources.retrieval_method: Pending public release; monitor project page.
sources.notes: Closest public match to our shot/rebound/block event taxonomy. Research-only until released with explicit terms.

sources.name: NSVA (NBA Sports Video Annotations)
sources.contents: NBA broadcast clips with fine-grained event captions; HF subset ~1,051 train / 265 val video-text pairs.
sources.size: Subset size on HF; full set requires download scripts.
sources.attribution_text: NSVA authors.
sources.retrieval_method: HF subset or repository download scripts; do not scrape NBA.com.
sources.notes: The repository scripts may point at NBA.com; the platform terms still prohibit scraping. Use only the HF subset or a licensed copy.

sources.name: SpaceJam
sources.contents: ~32,560 single-player 16-frame action clips with RGB frames and joint keypoints.
sources.license_id: Code MIT; clip content license unaddressed
sources.attribution_text: SpaceJam authors.
sources.retrieval_method: Google Drive link (donation-ware).
sources.notes: Useful for pose/action pretraining only if the clip provenance is cleared.

sources.name: Roboflow — BasketBall Dataset (test-datset/basketball-bs0zc)
sources.contents: 9,445 still images with object-detection boxes for 5 classes: ball, person, made, rim, shoot. One dataset version, updated 2023.
sources.size: Not published on the project page
sources.attribution_text: Cite 'BasketBall Dataset' by 'test datset', Roboflow Universe (2023).
sources.retrieval_method: Roboflow export after sign-in; choose COCO or YOLO format.
sources.notes: Still images only — no track IDs, no temporal events, no court mapping. The uploader account is named 'test datset' and the project has no description, so treat the CC-BY-4.0 tag as self-asserted until provenance is verified. Do not assume commercial clearance for the underlying footage.

sources.name: Roboflow Universe basketball projects (index)
sources.contents: Dozens of image datasets for ball, player, rim, and court detection; some video-derived frame sets.
sources.attribution_text: Per-project attribution required.
sources.retrieval_method: Roboflow account and export.
sources.notes: Verify the license tag on each project; not all are CC-BY. Best for bootstrapping still-image detectors, not continuous video.

sources.name: VRU_Basketball (AVS-VRU)
sources.contents: Three dynamic basketball court scenes (Guangzhou, Dongguan, Long360), 36 viewpoints each; 250 frames at 1080p or 700 frames at 4K.
sources.size: Multiple zip archives; exact size not verified.
sources.attribution_text: Wu et al., Swift4D (ICLR 2025) and LocalDyGS (ICCV 2025).
sources.retrieval_method: Hugging Face download.
sources.notes: Multi-view, calibrated-style footage is useful for homography and multi-view tracking research, but clips are short.

sources.name: UniqueData basketball_tracking
sources.contents: Broadcast screenshots with ball bounding boxes and occlusion/basket attributes; free sample of a paid commercial dataset.
sources.attribution_text: UniqueData / Unidata.pro.
sources.retrieval_method: Hugging Face download of the free sample; commercial license available from vendor.
sources.notes: ND license means no derivatives; use for evaluation only, not for building a redistributable dataset.

sources.name: APIDIS
sources.contents: ~2 hours from 7 viewpoints at ~22 fps / 1600x1200; calibration; ball/player/referee annotations for one minute; ball-possession and event annotations for the full game.
sources.attribution_text: APIDIS project, UCLouvain ISPGroup; cite related publications.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct download links from the project page.
sources.notes: Excellent for homography/calibration and ball tracking research. The old apidis.org domain is unreliable; use the GitLab page.

sources.name: Spiroudome
sources.contents: 8-camera basketball game at ~25 fps / 1600x1200; calibration to a common world frame; manually annotated player positions on camera 2.
sources.attribution_text: Spiroudome dataset, UCLouvain ISPGroup; cite related publications.
sources.retrieval_method: Kaggle dataset download.
sources.notes: Multi-view calibration and player-position ground truth; ideal for homography and tracking research.

sources.name: Pexels basketball stock videos
sources.contents: 5,232+ basketball stock clips, mostly amateur/pickup/stock footage.
sources.attribution_text: Not required; credit appreciated.
sources.retrieval_method: Manual or Pexels API download.
sources.notes: Commercially safe but not broadcast-authentic. Best for augmentation, pose/action pretraining, and UI demos.

sources.name: Pixabay basketball videos
sources.contents: Royalty-free basketball stock clips.
sources.attribution_text: Not required.
sources.retrieval_method: Manual or Pixabay API download.
sources.notes: Same profile as Pexels: commercially safe, not broadcast-authentic.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — safe-license basketball videos
sources.contents: Per-file basketball videos whose license is Public domain, CC0, or CC BY (no share-alike by default).
sources.size: Varies; discovery manifest caps each file at 100 MB by default.
sources.license_id: Per-file: Public domain, CC0, or CC BY
sources.attribution_text: Per-file; the generated manifest captures artist, page URL, and license.
sources.retrieval_method: MediaWiki API discovery plus direct upload.wikimedia.org download through scripts/data_ops.py.
sources.notes: Approved only for files whose per-file license is Public domain, CC0, or CC BY. Reject broadcast rips and unclear provenance. Share-alike is excluded by default.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Videos of basketball
sources.contents: Mixed collection of basketball videos; each file carries its own license.
sources.attribution_text: Per-file; capture title, author, source URL, license, and modification note.
sources.retrieval_method: Per-file download after license tag verification.
sources.notes: Commons policy requires commercial-use-compatible licenses, but mis-tagged uploads exist. Verify each file and avoid broadcast screenshots.

sources.name: Internet Archive basketball movies
sources.contents: ~71,000 basketball-related movie items; mixed home movies, school games, newsreels, and apparent broadcast rips.
sources.license_id: Per-item; Archive is not the licensor
sources.attribution_text: Per-item.
sources.retrieval_method: Per-item download after rights verification.
sources.notes: Use only items with credible PD/CC tags; skip broadcast rips, DVD transfers, and TV recordings.

sources.name: NBA / NCAA broadcast footage
sources.contents: League and broadcast video; owned and licensed by the league and its broadcast partners.
sources.license_id: NBA Terms of Use / broadcast licenses
sources.retrieval_method: DO NOT SCRAPE. Requires a direct license from the rights holder.
sources.notes: Research-only datasets derived from broadcast footage do not grant us a license to the underlying video.

sources.name: Roboflow - NBA Ball Detection (cps-etiji), v1
sources.contents: 1,288 images, single class `basketball`, YOLO-format boxes, 640x640.
sources.attribution_text: NBA Ball Detection dataset, cps-etiji, Roboflow Universe (CC BY 4.0).
sources.retrieval_method: Roboflow Universe export, YOLO format.
sources.notes: Licence is CC BY 4.0 as asserted by the uploader, but the frames are broadcast footage, so underlying rights are unverified - hence CAUTION and self-asserted provenance rather than SAFE/verified. Only 2 distinct source videos. Both of them appear in train, valid AND test, so every metric from this dataset is same-video leakage: our YOLO11m scored 0.914 here but 0.270 on an unseen game. Do not use its val split to claim generalisation.

sources.name: Roboflow - Basketball Players (roboflow-universe-projects), v25
sources.contents: 1,196 images, 9 classes (Ball, Hoop, Period, Player, Ref, Shot Clock, Team Name, Team Points, Time Remaining), YOLO format.
sources.attribution_text: Basketball Players dataset, roboflow-universe-projects, Roboflow Universe (CC BY 4.0).
sources.retrieval_method: Roboflow Universe export, YOLO format.
sources.notes: PROVENANCE FLAG. The dataset licence says CC BY 4.0, but the frame filenames reveal the underlying footage: about 980 of 1,140 train frames are named `youtube-<frame>`, so the source is an unnamed YouTube upload, and the other 160 are an Iowa-Nebraska college broadcast. A Roboflow dataset licence cannot grant rights the uploader did not hold. All permissions left null pending a human decision. 2 distinct source videos.

sources.name: YouTube basketball batch (agent download, 2026-10-20)
sources.contents: Basketball videos downloaded for ball-detector training and full-game analysis: 6 full/partial games (Pahoa JV, Lima Senior, Bellingham, Nepal U19, Kansas State scrimmage, PC Friars scrimmage) plus 7 short clips. Per-video metadata in data/raw/youtube-basketball-2026-10-20/2026-10-20/ingest_manifest.json.
sources.size: 8.78 GB, 13 video files (6 full/partial games, 7 short clips)
sources.retrieval_method: Agent download; per-video ingest_manifest.json records URL, channel, upload date, duration, resolution, and SHA-256
sources.notes: Research training only; includes full games. Per-video license is unrecorded. Nothing in this batch is released or redistributed. Prefer official league/school channels for new downloads. Promote to CAUTION/SAFE only after per-video rights review.
